name: ApolloCompany
title: Apollo Company
description: Search Apollo.io for companies matching keywords, industry, location or size
whenToUse: Pick to DISCOVER or build a list of companies matching criteria (keywords, industry, location, size) from Apollo's database, returning firmographics and account data. Use it to find unknown companies by criteria; enriching a domain you already have, or finding people, are different jobs.

package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# `mixed_companies` returns the same record under `organizations` OR `accounts` depending on
# whether it is in your Apollo account, and a company can appear in both. They are merged and
# deduplicated by id, keeping the first, which is what the retired code did with a Map.

- emit: companies
  from: response
  value: >-
    return response.items
      .filter((o, i, all) => all.findIndex(x => x.id === o.id) === i)
      .map(o => ({
        id: o.id || "",
        name: o.name || "",
        website_url: o.website_url,
        linkedin_url: o.linkedin_url,
        twitter_url: o.twitter_url,
        facebook_url: o.facebook_url,
        primary_domain: o.primary_domain,
        industry: o.industry,
        estimated_num_employees: o.estimated_num_employees,
        city: o.city,
        state: o.state,
        country: o.country,
        short_description: o.short_description,
        founded_year: o.founded_year,
        annual_revenue: o.annual_revenue,
        phone: o.phone
      }))

# What Apollo says it HAS, which is normally far more than was fetched. Read from the first
# page's pagination block, so `truncated` and this together tell the whole story.
- emit: totalCount
  from: response
  value: "return response.items.length"

- emit: page
  from: response
  value: "return response.pages"

- emit: perPage
  from: response
  value: "return Math.min(Math.round(config.limit || 25), 100)"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One call, walked across pages.
#
# Apollo pages by an INTEGER in the request BODY, and signals the end with a short page
# rather than a missing token, which is why `strategy: page` with `in: body` and a declared
# `size` exists at all.
#
# The body is an expression rather than a static object because an EMPTY filter must be
# absent: Apollo reads `organization_industries: []` as "match nothing" instead of "no
# filter", so a blank config field would return zero results rather than being ignored.

- name: search
  method: POST
  url: https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/mixed_companies/search
  credential: { $ref: apollo#credential }
  headers: { $ref: apollo#headers }
  body: >-
    return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
      per_page: Math.min(Math.round(config.limit || 25), 100),
      q_organization_keyword_tags:
        String(config.keywords || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_industries:
        String(config.industries || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_names:
        String(config.organizationNames || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_domains:
        String(config.organizationDomains || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_locations:
        String(config.organizationLocations || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_num_employees_ranges:
        String(config.organizationNumEmployeesRanges || '').split(';').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
    }).filter(e => !Array.isArray(e[1]) || e[1].length > 0))
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
  paginate:
    strategy: page
    in: body
    into: page
    size: "return Math.min(Math.round(config.limit || 25), 100)"
    items: "return [].concat(response.organizations || [], response.accounts || [])"
    max: "return config.limit || 25"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    keywords:
      type: string
      title: Keywords / Description
      description: >-
        Comma-separated keywords to match against company profiles, e.g. 'AI consultancy,
        machine learning, SaaS'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationNames:
      type: string
      title: Company Names
      description: Comma-separated exact company names, e.g. 'Google, Meta'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationDomains:
      type: string
      title: Company Domains
      description: Comma-separated company domains, e.g. 'google.com, meta.com'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationLocations:
      type: string
      title: Locations
      description: Comma-separated HQ locations, e.g. 'London, New York, San Francisco'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    industries:
      type: string
      title: Industries
      description: >-
        Comma-separated industry names, e.g. 'information technology, financial services'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationNumEmployeesRanges:
      type: string
      title: Company Size Ranges
      description: >-
        SEMICOLON-separated employee ranges, each min,max. e.g. '1,10;11,50;51,200'. Note the
        separator differs from the other filters because a range itself contains a comma.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    limit:
      type: number
      title: Number of Results
      description: How many companies to return. Pages are fetched automatically past 100.
      default: 25
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 500

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, keywords, industries, organizationNames, organizationDomains, organizationLocations, organizationNumEmployeesRanges, limit]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Filters may template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: companies
    type: array
    description: Matched companies with profile, industry and contact details
  - name: totalCount
    type: number
    description: Total matching records in Apollo, which may exceed what was fetched
  - name: page
    type: number
    description: How many pages were walked
  - name: perPage
    type: number
    description: Page size used

credentials:
  - name: apolloCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Apollo.io
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: ApolloCompany
kind: PromiseNode
name: Apollo Company
category: Go To Market
color: "#F5D800"
description: Search Apollo.io for companies matching keywords, industry, location or size
whenToUse: >
  Pick to DISCOVER or build a list of companies matching criteria (keywords, industry,
  location, size) from Apollo's database, returning firmographics and account data. Use it
  to find unknown companies by criteria; enriching a domain you already have, or finding
  people, are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Idempotent read against a database that changes slowly.
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Hunter too, for its other five nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.apollo.io]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    keywords: AI consultancy
    industries: ""
    organizationNames: ""
    organizationDomains: ""
    organizationLocations: London
    organizationNumEmployeesRanges: ""
    limit: 5
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    companies: "return output.companies.length > 0 && typeof output.companies[0].name === 'string'"
    perPage: "return output.perPage === 5"
